papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics of Ciona adult brains reveals functional zonalization and insights into neural gland function.
papers.abstract: The ascidian Ciona is a pivotal chordate model for illuminating the evolutionary origins of the vertebrate brain. Here, spatial transcriptomics of the adult Ciona neural complex, combined with image-based computational super-resolution mapping, resolved distinct tissue domains including the cerebral ganglion, neural gland, ciliated funnel, neural gland duct/dorsal strand, and body wall muscle. Within the cerebral ganglion, high-resolution mapping revealed clear molecular zonalization separating the cortex and medulla, alongside regional specialization within the cortex itself. The neural gland
papers.summary: This study applies spatial transcriptomics to the adult neural complex of the ascidian Ciona, resolving distinct tissue domains including the cerebral ganglion, neural gland, and associated structures. High-resolution mapping revealed molecular zonalization within the cerebral ganglion, separating cortex and medulla and showing regional specialization within the cortex. The findings provide evolutionary insights into vertebrate brain origins and neural gland function.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics reveal impaired metabolic liver zonation in acute-on-chronic liver failure.
papers.abstract: Extrahepatic organ failures are key determinants of acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF). While the role of systemic inflammation and mitochondrial dysfunction in the pathogenesis of ACLF is well known, the contribution of the liver itself is less understood. We therefore performed transcriptome and functional analyses of the liver in order to identify hepatic drivers of ACLF.
papers.summary: This study uses spatial transcriptomics to map gene expression across liver zones in patients with acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF), revealing that the liver's normal metabolic zonation—the spatial division of metabolic functions—becomes impaired. The findings suggest that this loss of zonal organization within the liver itself contributes to the disease, beyond the well-known roles of systemic inflammation and mitochondrial dysfunction.

papers.title: highSpaClone enables copy number alteration inference and tumor subclone analysis for high-resolution spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: High-resolution spatially resolved transcriptomics (SRT) offers unprecedented opportunities to investigate tumor heterogeneity but poses substantial computational and analytical challenges. Here, we present highSpaClone, a computational framework for copy number alteration (CNA) inference and tumor subclone identification from high-resolution SRT data across multiple spatial scales. By integrating spatial constraints into CNA estimation and clonal clustering, highSpaClone enables neighboring spatial locations to share information, thereby improving the robustness of genomic signals and the acc
papers.summary: highSpaClone is a computational framework that infers copy number alterations and identifies tumor subclones from high-resolution spatial transcriptomics data. It incorporates spatial constraints into CNA estimation and clonal clustering, allowing neighboring spatial locations to share information and improving the robustness of genomic signals and subclone detection across multiple spatial scales.

papers.title: Pan-cancer screening and integrative multi-omics and deep learning reveal the prognostic significance of an IBD-CRC shared host-microbe signature in bladder urothelial carcinoma.
papers.abstract: The prognostic relevance of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD)-colorectal cancer (CRC) shared host-microbe signatures in non-intestinal epithelial malignancies remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic and biological significance of an IBD-CRC shared host-microbe interactome signature in bladder urothelial carcinoma (BLCA).
papers.summary: This study investigates whether a host-microbe interaction signature previously linked to both inflammatory bowel disease and colorectal cancer also has prognostic value in bladder urothelial carcinoma, a non-intestinal cancer. Using pan-cancer screening combined with multi-omics integration and deep learning, the authors identify and characterize this shared signature in BLCA, suggesting its biological and clinical relevance extends beyond intestinal malignancies.

papers.title: Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomics Define Eosinophil Heterogeneity during Influenza A Virus-induced Exacerbation of Fungal Allergic Asthma in C57BL/6 mice.
papers.abstract: Although eosinophils are accepted as transcriptionally heterogeneous in asthma, how allergic inflammation shapes eosinophil states during influenza A virus (IAV) infection remains undefined. We integrated high-resolution single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, quantitative immunofluorescence imaging, and cell-cell communication analyses to profile murine lungs across naïve, asthma, influenza (Flu), and Asthma+Flu conditions. We identified three related eosinophil transcriptional states distributed along a disease-associated continuum. Eosinophils in the Flu-only condition preferen
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics to profile eosinophil heterogeneity in mouse lungs across naive, asthma, influenza, and combined asthma+influenza conditions. The authors identify three related eosinophil transcriptional states along a disease-associated continuum, with distinct state preferences depending on the disease context. The work reveals how influenza A virus infection reshapes eosinophil states during allergic asthma exacerbation.

papers.title: Integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analysis reveals an epithelial cell-derived prognostic and immunotherapeutic signature with ADAM12 as a key functional regulator in non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.abstract: This study developed a Prognostic and Immunotherapeutic Signature (PIS) for NSCLC using single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data. By integrating TCGA and GEO datasets with machine learning, we identified key epithelial cells-related genes predictive of immunotherapy response. PIS effectively stratifies patients by survival and immune activity, with low-PIS individuals showing better outcomes and higher immune infiltration. We confirmed the high expression of ADAM12 in both tissue samples and cell lines, and validated its functional roles through cellular assays. Furthermore, mouse model experiments d
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data from NSCLC patients to build a Prognostic and Immunotherapeutic Signature (PIS) based on epithelial cell-related genes, using machine learning to predict immunotherapy response and survival. The signature stratifies patients by outcome and immune activity, and the authors validate ADAM12 as a key functional regulator through cell line assays and mouse experiments.

papers.title: Adrenomedullin from spinal cord injury drives heterotopic ossification in skeletal muscle via a neuro-immune-bone axis.
papers.abstract: Neurological heterotopic ossification can rapidly arise in the periarticular muscles following spinal cord injury. However, the specific mechanism of how the injured central nervous system regulates heterotopic bone formation in peripheral tissues remains largely unexplored. Here we first demonstrate through single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomic analysis that fibroadipogenic progenitor cells (FAPs) contribute to heterotopic ossification in injured muscle tissues following spinal cord injury. Mechanistically, we define a neuro-immune-bone axis in which endothelial tip cells with
papers.summary: This study shows that spinal cord injury triggers heterotopic ossification in periarticular skeletal muscle through a neuro-immune-bone axis. Using single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics, the authors identify fibroadipogenic progenitor cells (FAPs) as the source of ectopic bone and implicate adrenomedullin from injured spinal cord and endothelial tip cells in driving this process.

papers.title: FABP4 characterizes metabolic-immune interactions and serves as a prognostic biomarker across gynecologic malignancies: a multi-omics integrative analysis.
papers.abstract: Gynecological malignancies-including breast, cervical, ovarian, endometrial cancers and uterine sarcoma-pose a serious threat to women's health owing to their high incidence, aggressiveness and frequent recurrence. Fatty acid-binding protein 4 (FABP4) is a key regulator of lipid metabolism and tumor metabolic reprogramming, yet systematic investigations of its role across gynecological malignancies remain scarce. Here, by integrating data from TCGA, GTEx and multiple public repositories, we performed a multi-omics, multi-scale analysis of five gynecological malignancies, encompassing transcrip
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data from TCGA, GTEx, and other public repositories to systematically characterize the role of FABP4 across five gynecological malignancies (breast, cervical, ovarian, endometrial cancers, and uterine sarcoma). The authors find that FABP4 is linked to metabolic-immune interactions and serves as a prognostic biomarker across these cancers. The work highlights FABP4 as a potential cross-cancer biomarker and therapeutic target.

papers.title: Cell-based therapies of autoimmune diseases in the context of artificial intelligence development.
papers.abstract: Autoimmune diseases are comprised of several chronic inflammatory conditions characterized by activation of autoreactive T and B lymphocytes and produces autoantibodies. While most of the current treatment options mainly rely on non-specific immunosuppression, stem cell based therapies can be a promising candidate for promoting "immune reset" and restore long term tolerance against these complex diseases. Stem cell based therapy eliminate autoreactive clones and reconstitute immune tolerance. Besides, mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs; also referred to as mesenchymal stem cells) have immunomodul
papers.summary: This review examines cell-based therapies, particularly stem cell and mesenchymal stromal cell approaches, for treating autoimmune diseases by promoting immune reset and restoring long-term tolerance rather than relying on non-specific immunosuppression. It also discusses how artificial intelligence could be integrated into the development and optimization of these therapies.

papers.title: Vaping reorganizes the pulmonary macrophage landscape into multiple sex-dimorphic microenvironments.
papers.abstract: Pulmonary macrophages are central orchestrators of inflammatory resolution and tissue repair in the lung. Whether vaping-associated macrophage dysregulation is spatially organized, sex-dimorphic, or detectable by bulk transcriptomic approaches remains poorly understood.
papers.summary: This study examines how vaping alters the landscape of pulmonary macrophages, the immune cells that manage inflammation and lung repair. The authors find that vaping reorganizes these macrophages into multiple distinct microenvironments that differ between males and females, and that these spatial and sex-specific changes are not well captured by standard bulk transcriptomic methods.

papers.title: Realistic coupling enables flexible macroscopic traveling waves in the mouse cortex.
papers.abstract: Traveling waves are ubiquitous in neuronal systems across different spatial scales. While microscopic and mesoscopic waves are relatively well studied, the emergence of macroscopic traveling waves remains less understood. Here, by modeling the mouse cortex using spatial transcriptomic and connectivity data, we show that realistic cortical connectivity can generate a significantly higher level of macroscopic traveling waves than artificial local and uniform connectivity across multiple oscillation frequency bands, with the strongest advantage appearing in the theta, alpha, and beta frequency ba
papers.summary: Using spatial transcriptomic and connectivity data to model the mouse cortex, the authors show that realistic cortical connectivity produces far more macroscopic traveling waves than artificial local or uniform connectivity, especially in theta, alpha, and beta bands. This suggests that the brain's actual wiring architecture is key to generating large-scale wave dynamics.

papers.title: Machine learning identifies ac4C-related prognostic signature and TUBA1C as therapeutic target in COAD.
papers.abstract: To explore the role of N4-acetylcytidine (ac4C)-related genes (acRGs) in colon adenocarcinoma (COAD) and identify reliable prognostic biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets. Multi-source transcriptomic datasets (TCGA-COAD, GSE39582, GSE17536) and single-cell RNA-seq data were analyzed. Ten machine learning algorithms were integrated to construct an acRG-based prognostic signature (acRGBS). Immune microenvironment (TME) and genomic profiling were performed, with in vitro functional experiments validating TUBA1C's role. acRGBS, comprising four hub genes (SARAF, CDC42SE2, TSPYL2, TUBA1C), e
papers.journal: Mammalian genome : official journal of the International Mammalian Genome Society
papers.summary: This study used multi-source transcriptomic and single-cell RNA-seq data with ten integrated machine learning algorithms to build a prognostic signature based on N4-acetylcytidine (ac4C)-related genes in colon adenocarcinoma. The four-gene signature (SARAF, CDC42SE2, TSPYL2, TUBA1C) stratifies patients by prognosis and links to immune microenvironment and genomic features, with in vitro experiments validating TUBA1C as a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: T cell-derived CCL5 drives macrophage immunometabolic remodeling in chronic prostatitis via the CCR5-ERK-PKM2/HIF-1α axis.
papers.abstract: Chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome (CP/CPPS) affects millions of men, yet the immune circuits that sustain sterile prostatic inflammation and pain remain poorly defined. Here we identify a T cell-macrophage metabolic signaling axis that drives chronic prostatitis. Integrated analysis of mouse experimental autoimmune prostatitis, chronically inflamed human prostate tissue, single-cell transcriptomes and spatial profiles revealed a population of glycolytic, HIF-1α-activated inflammatory macrophages enriched in diseased prostate niches. T cell-derived CCL5 was markedly induced and s
papers.summary: This study identifies a T cell-macrophage signaling axis driving chronic prostatitis, where T cell-derived CCL5 activates macrophages through CCR5-ERK-PKM2/HIF-1α signaling, promoting glycolytic and inflammatory macrophage reprogramming in diseased prostate tissue. The findings integrate mouse models, human tissue, single-cell transcriptomics, and spatial profiling to reveal this immunometabolic circuit as a potential therapeutic target for chronic pelvic pain syndrome.

papers.title: Image-guided alignment of consecutive multi-modal tissue slides.
papers.abstract: We present COAST (consecutive multi-omics alignment of spatial tissues), a method to reliably physically align consecutive tissue sections to produce a unified multi-modal molecular dataset suitable for downstream applications. COAST relies exclusively on the images associated with spatial data, eliminating the need for common molecular features or prior annotations. We demonstrate the effectiveness of COAST using spatial transcriptomics slides from different technologies, tissues, and resolutions, in which it achieves performance comparable to established uni-modal alignment tools. Applying C
papers.summary: COAST is a new computational method that physically aligns consecutive tissue sections using only their associated images, enabling the creation of unified multi-modal spatial datasets without requiring shared molecular features or prior annotations. The authors demonstrate its effectiveness across spatial transcriptomics slides from different technologies, tissues, and resolutions, achieving performance comparable to established uni-modal alignment tools.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell and machine learning analysis identifies a tumor doubling time-related prognostic signature and therapeutic targets in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) exhibits marked molecular heterogeneity and diverse clinical outcomes, partly influenced by HPV status and the tumor immune microenvironment. Although tumor doubling time (TDT) reflects tumor growth kinetics and has prognostic relevance, its molecular basis in HNSCC remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell RNA sequencing with machine learning to identify a gene signature associated with tumor doubling time (TDT) in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. The authors link this TDT-related signature to prognosis and propose potential therapeutic targets, while accounting for HPV status and the tumor immune microenvironment. The work suggests that tumor growth kinetics can be captured molecularly and may inform patient stratification.

papers.title: A systematic benchmark of bioinformatics methods for single-cell and spatial RNA-seq nanopore long reads data.
papers.abstract: Alternative splicing plays a crucial role in transcriptomic complexity, yet remains difficult to resolve at the single-cell level due to the limitations of short-read technologies. Coupling single-cell with long-read sequencing offers full-length transcript coverage, enabling more accurate isoform detection. Diverse computational tools tailored for single-cell and spatial long-read transcriptomics have been developed. To compare the effectiveness of these approaches, we generated paired short-read and Nanopore long-read single-cell datasets, tailored for benchmarking bioinformatics tools. We e
papers.summary: This paper benchmarks computational tools for analyzing single-cell and spatial RNA-seq data generated with Nanopore long-read sequencing, which enables full-length transcript and isoform detection. The authors generated paired short-read and long-read single-cell datasets to systematically compare tool performance. The work provides guidance on method selection for isoform-level single-cell transcriptomics.

papers.title: Interpretable multi-omics integration across mixed-order tensors with MANTRA.
papers.abstract: The integration of multi-modal molecular data is crucial for understanding complex diseases, but existing methods struggle with modern experimental designs that generate datasets with mixed-order tensors-for example, a third-order drug-response tensor alongside a second-order transcriptomics matrix. Here, we present MANTRA (Multi-view ANalysis with Tensor and matRix Alignment), a probabilistic framework that integrates collections of tensors of different orders, combining the strengths of group factor analysis and tensor decomposition. MANTRA learns interpretable latent factors and naturally h
papers.summary: MANTRA is a probabilistic framework that integrates multi-omics datasets of different tensor orders (e.g., third-order drug-response tensors and second-order transcriptomics matrices) by combining group factor analysis with tensor decomposition. It learns interpretable latent factors that capture shared and modality-specific variation across mixed-order data, addressing a gap in existing integration methods.

papers.title: Alignment-free integration of single-nucleus ATAC-seq across species with sPYce.
papers.abstract: Changes in gene regulation largely contribute to differences in cellular identities and phenotypes between species. Single-nucleus assays for transposase-accessible chromatin with sequencing (snATAC-seq) are an efficient strategy to identify putative gene regulatory elements and provide new insight into evolutionary divergence of regulatory programmes. However, no dedicated framework exists to integrate and compare snATAC-seq data across species, while methods designed for single-cell gene expression data have serious limitations. Here we present sPYce, a cross-species snATAC-seq integration m
papers.summary: sPYce is a new computational framework for integrating single-nucleus ATAC-seq data across species without requiring sequence alignment, addressing a gap since existing methods were designed for single-cell gene expression data. It enables comparison of chromatin accessibility and regulatory programs between species, offering new insight into the evolutionary divergence of gene regulation.

papers.title: High-Content CRISPR Screening: Methods and Applications.
papers.abstract: Clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR)-Cas9 screening has become a central technology in functional genomics, enabling genome-scale interrogation via pooled perturbations. Early CRISPR screens employed survival or simple phenotypic readouts to identify essential genes and drug resistance mechanisms. However, as biological questions have shifted toward understanding regulatory networks, cellular heterogeneity, and context-dependent gene functions, there has been increasing demand for screening strategies capable of capturing complex cellular phenotypes beyond cell fi
papers.summary: This review covers high-content CRISPR screening, an approach that combines CRISPR-based gene perturbation with microscopy or other imaging readouts to capture complex cellular phenotypes. It discusses how the field has moved beyond simple survival-based screens toward methods that can probe regulatory networks, cellular heterogeneity, and context-dependent gene functions.

papers.title: Increased Amyloidogenic Neuronal Injury in HIV-1-infected APP-KI Alzheimer's disease mice.
papers.abstract: A higher incidence of dementia, including Alzheimer's-like pathology, is observed in aged people living with human immunodeficiency virus-1 (HIV-1). However, mechanisms linking HIV-1 to Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology remain unclear, due to the lack of animal models that allow for concurrent studies of HIV-1 and AD.
papers.journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
papers.summary: This study develops a mouse model combining HIV-1 infection with Alzheimer's disease-like pathology (APP-KI mice) to investigate how HIV-1 may accelerate or exacerbate amyloid-related neuronal injury. The authors report increased amyloidogenic neuronal damage in HIV-1-infected APP-KI mice, suggesting a mechanistic link between HIV-1 and AD-like pathology. This provides a new animal model for studying the intersection of HIV-1 and Alzheimer's disease.

papers.title: Decoding cell-cell communication in spatial transcriptomics: mechanistic insights, modeling constraints, and analytical caveats.
papers.abstract: Cell-cell communication (CCC) is essential for maintaining tissue organization and driving biological progression, yet its inference from transcriptomic data has long been limited by the absence of spatial context. Advances in spatial transcriptomics (ST) now enable mechanistically grounded analyses of CCC by preserving the physical organization of cells and their microenvironments. In this review, we examine recent methodological developments in CCC inference from ST data, focusing on how statistical, optimal transport, and deep learning frameworks incorporate spatial information to model lig
papers.summary: This review examines recent computational methods for inferring cell-cell communication from spatial transcriptomics data, covering statistical, optimal transport, and deep learning frameworks that incorporate spatial context. It highlights mechanistic insights gained, modeling constraints, and analytical caveats that researchers should consider when interpreting such inferences.

papers.title: EGFR-Mutant Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer With Small Cell Transformation: Clinicopathological Features, Treatment Landscape, and Biomarker Profiles.
papers.abstract: Transformed small-cell lung cancer (tSCLC) is a clinically important resistance mechanism to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors in EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer. This study characterizes clinical features, treatment outcomes, and biomarker profiles in patients with tSCLC.
papers.summary: This study characterizes the clinical and pathological features, treatment outcomes, and biomarker profiles of patients whose EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer transformed into small cell lung cancer (tSCLC), a key resistance mechanism to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors. It provides a comprehensive picture of this aggressive transformation to help guide clinical management and identify potential biomarkers.

papers.title: Dietary Polyphenol Acteoside-Related Molecular Signatures in Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma: Multi-Omics Profiling and Functional Validation of IMPDH1.
papers.abstract: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is characterized by substantial metabolic and molecular heterogeneity, but the disease-relevant programs associated with acteoside, a dietary polyphenol, remain poorly understood. We integrated predicted acteoside targets with bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomic data from ccRCC and combined molecular subtyping with cross-cohort machine-learning analysis. Acteoside-related signatures were preferentially enriched in malignant compartments and increased with tumor grade and stage. Consensus clustering identified two molecular subtypes with distinc
papers.summary: This study integrates predicted acteoside targets with bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics to define acteoside-related molecular signatures in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC). The signatures are enriched in malignant compartments and correlate with tumor grade and stage, and consensus clustering reveals two molecular subtypes. Functional validation highlights IMPDH1 as a key player in these acteoside-associated programs.

papers.title: Amplification bias in sequencing-based spatial transcriptomics: sources, mechanisms, impacts, and mitigation strategies.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) has emerged as a powerful approach for profiling gene expression in spatial tissue context; yet, its quantitative accuracy remains substantially compromised by amplification bias introduced during the complex library preparation process. These biases arise at multiple stages and accumulate throughout the experimental workflow, distorting transcript abundance, reducing detection sensitivity, and ultimately confounding downstream spatial analyses. This review systematically analyzes amplification bias in ST. We examine how input templates, oligonucleotide components
papers.summary: This review systematically examines amplification bias in sequencing-based spatial transcriptomics, tracing how biases arise from input templates, oligonucleotide components, and library preparation steps, and how they accumulate to distort transcript abundance and spatial analyses. It also surveys mitigation strategies to improve quantitative accuracy in ST experiments.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell sequencing and machine learning analyses identify chronic inflammation and cancer-associated fibroblast subsets as drivers of adverse outcomes in ovarian cancer.
papers.abstract: Ovarian cancer remains the deadliest gynecological malignancy, with neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) often leaving residual fibroblast-enriched disease.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell sequencing data with machine learning to dissect the ovarian cancer microenvironment, focusing on how chronic inflammation and specific cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF) subsets drive poor outcomes after neoadjuvant chemotherapy. The authors identify CAF subpopulations and inflammatory signatures associated with residual disease and adverse prognosis, highlighting potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Stage-specific ROMO1 in rheumatoid arthritis: predictive immune insights into the MIF pathway and HLA-DR/IL2RA axis via integrated GWAS, transcriptomic, single-cell, and spatial profiling.
papers.abstract: Emerging evidence links reactive oxygen species modulator 1 (ROMO1), a key mitochondrial ROS regulator, to rheumatoid arthritis (RA) pathogenesis. However, its exact mechanism remains elusive given the conflicting evidence about its specific function. We used a four-level integrative framework combining multi-omics data and literature‑supported mechanistic inference. At the genetic level, Mendelian randomization (MR) was performed to explore potential causal relationships between ROMO1, IL2RA, HLA-DR, MIF, and RA risk, followed by differential expression analysis and machine learning-based fea
papers.summary: This study integrates GWAS, transcriptomic, single-cell, and spatial data to investigate the role of ROMO1 in rheumatoid arthritis, identifying stage-specific expression patterns and links to the MIF pathway and HLA-DR/IL2RA axis. Using Mendelian randomization and machine learning, the authors propose ROMO1 as a predictive immune marker with potential stage-dependent functions in RA pathogenesis.

papers.title: Benchmarking cell type annotation in spatial transcriptomics: resolving cellular hierarchies, biological fidelity, and dynamic cell states.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics enables the quantification of gene expression within its native tissue context, providing unprecedented insight into tissue architecture, cellular ecosystems, and local cell-cell interactions at regional and single-cell resolution. Accurate cell type annotation is a critical prerequisite for interpreting these data and is often the first and most essential step in downstream analysis. Despite rapid advances in computational methods, cell type annotation remains challenging and frequently requires extensive expert-driven manual curation based on marker-gene expression, s
papers.summary: This paper benchmarks computational methods for cell type annotation in spatial transcriptomics data, focusing on how well they resolve cellular hierarchies, preserve biological fidelity, and capture dynamic cell states. It highlights that despite rapid methodological advances, accurate annotation still often depends on expert manual curation using marker genes.

papers.title: Multimodal Analysis Reveals Aberrant Expression of SUMO2 and Its Significant Association With Key Mechanisms of Metabolic Pathways in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the third leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide. However, the role of small ubiquitin-like modifier 2 (SUMO2), a core member of the small ubiquitin-like modifier (SUMO) family, regarding its expression patterns and metabolism-related functions in HCC remains inadequately understood.
papers.summary: This study uses multimodal analysis to examine SUMO2 expression in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), finding that it is aberrantly expressed and linked to key metabolic pathway mechanisms. The findings suggest SUMO2 may play a role in HCC metabolism and could serve as a potential biomarker or therapeutic target.

papers.title: A categorization of spatial transcriptomics methods for cell-cell communication analysis.
papers.abstract: Cell-cell communication (CCC) is involved in regulating cellular behavior in tissues. Spatial transcriptomics adds local context to gene expression, enabling more biologically grounded CCC inference than single-cell RNA-seq alone. Rapid method development has yielded diverse CCC methods, each addressing distinct biological questions through varied analytical frameworks. We review 33 recent methods and organize them into three categories: inference of communication networks at cell-type or single-cell resolution, modeling of microenvironment-driven transcriptional variability and regulatory mod
papers.summary: This review categorizes 33 recent spatial transcriptomics methods for analyzing cell-cell communication (CCC) into three groups: cell-type or single-cell resolution network inference, modeling of microenvironment-driven transcriptional variability, and regulatory modulation. It provides a framework to help researchers select appropriate CCC methods based on the biological question and spatial resolution.

papers.title: Peripheral blood cells and immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis: a retrospective clinical study with pharmacovigilance and single-cell analysis.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-associated myocarditis (ICI-M) is a rare but potentially lethal immune-related adverse event (irAE). Early identification of fulminant (severe) cases remains challenging, and the peripheral immune derangements underlying ICI-M are incompletely characterized.
papers.summary: This retrospective clinical study investigates peripheral blood cell patterns in patients with immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis (ICI-M), a rare but potentially fatal side effect of cancer immunotherapy. By combining pharmacovigilance data with single-cell analysis, the authors aim to identify early markers of severe (fulminant) cases and characterize the immune cell changes in the blood that underlie this condition.

papers.title: An hiPSC-derived multi-lineage lung model exhibiting proximal-distal epithelial features for modeling pulmonary fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive and irreversible interstitial lung disease with limited therapeutic options. Existing hiPSC-derived lung organoid models are largely restricted to single epithelial lineages and cannot endogenously integrate multiple pulmonary cell types, limiting mechanistic studies and drug screening.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: The authors developed a human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived lung model that contains multiple epithelial cell lineages with both proximal and distal airway features, overcoming the single-lineage limitation of prior lung organoid systems. This multi-lineage model can be used to study pulmonary fibrosis mechanisms and screen potential drugs in a more physiologically relevant context.

papers.title: Multi-omics mapping of PSC genetic risk to a high TWAS-active JAML+ lipid-associated macrophage program: bridging single-cell heterogeneity, spatial fibrotic niches, and machine learning selection.
papers.abstract: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a chronic cholestatic liver disease with progressive peribiliary inflammation and fibrosis. Disease-modifying therapies are lacking, and the cell-type-specific mechanisms linking genetic susceptibility to pathogenic immune states remain incompletely understood.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data to map primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) genetic risk variants to a specific immune cell program—JAML+ lipid-associated macrophages—that shows high transcriptome-wide association activity. By combining single-cell heterogeneity, spatial fibrotic niche mapping, and machine learning, the authors link genetic susceptibility to a pathogenic macrophage state in the diseased liver. The work provides a framework for identifying cell-type-specific therapeutic targets in PSC.

papers.title: Single-cell transcriptomics and a boundary wound model reveal temporal decoupling and microenvironmental heterogeneity in radiation-induced fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Radiotherapy is a key treatment method for cancer, but high-dose treatment can lead to damage to normal tissues and chronic fibrosis. There is a lack of systematic temporal analysis of the dynamic progression from early damage signals to late extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell transcriptomics combined with a boundary wound model to track how radiation-induced fibrosis develops over time. The authors find that early damage signaling and later extracellular matrix deposition are temporally decoupled, and that the fibrotic microenvironment is heterogeneous across different cell populations and regions. This provides a more systematic temporal map of the transition from acute radiation damage to chronic fibrosis.

papers.title: Benchmarking computational decontamination of ambient RNA.
papers.abstract: Gene expression profiling of single cells using single-cell and single-nucleus RNA sequencing (sxRNA-seq) enables researchers to characterize cellular heterogeneity and unraveling complex biological processes at unprecedented resolution. However, sxRNA-seq faces challenges due to the presence of ambient RNA, extraneous RNA molecules not originating from the cells of interest. Sample preparation is a major source of ambient RNA, where harsh conditions can lead to cell lysis and the release of intracellular RNA. This inescapable inclusion of ambient RNA can cause erroneous results and hinder dow
papers.summary: This paper benchmarks computational methods for removing ambient RNA contamination from single-cell and single-nucleus RNA sequencing data. Ambient RNA, released from lysed cells during sample preparation, can distort gene expression profiles and lead to false biological conclusions. The study systematically compares existing decontamination tools to guide researchers in choosing appropriate approaches.

papers.title: Multi-omics identification of MBNL2 associated with poor pathological response to neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy in lung squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy (NACI) improves outcomes in resectable lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC), yet response varies widely and current biomarkers lack precision. Novel correlates of immunotherapy sensitivity tailored to the LUSC tumor microenvironment (TME) are urgently needed.
papers.summary: This study uses multi-omics profiling to identify MBNL2 as a biomarker associated with poor pathological response to neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy in lung squamous cell carcinoma. The finding suggests MBNL2 could help stratify patients likely to benefit from this treatment approach.

papers.title: Bulk and single cell RNA sequencing data reveal lactylation-related gene signatures for prognosis and immunity in cervical cancer.
papers.abstract: Previous studies indicate that lactylation, a post-translational modification, may play an important role in the progression of cervical cancer (CC). However, the comprehensive roles of lactylation in influencing the tumor microenvironment, immune landscape, and prognosis of CC have yet to be fully elucidated. The bulk RNA-seq and single-cell RNA-seq datasets of CC patients were downloaded from the Cancer Genome Atlas and Gene Expression Omnibus databases, respectively. A total of 630 genes associated with lactylation activity were identified using AUCell algorithm, differential expression, an
papers.journal: Brazilian journal of medical and biological research = Revista brasileira de pesquisas medicas e biologicas
papers.summary: This study analyzed bulk and single-cell RNA-seq data from cervical cancer patients to identify lactylation-related gene signatures associated with prognosis and immune landscape. Using the AUCell algorithm, they identified 630 lactylation-associated genes and developed a prognostic signature linking lactylation activity to tumor microenvironment and immune features. The findings suggest lactylation may serve as a biomarker and therapeutic target in cervical cancer.

papers.title: EMCN is associated with vascular-immune crosstalk and represents a potential biomarker in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: While MUC family genes have been established as prognostic biomarkers in gastric cancer, and GWAS studies link EMCN mutations to chemotherapy-induced myelosuppression in NSCLC, the systematic characterization of EMCN in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains elusive.
papers.summary: This study investigates the gene EMCN in lung adenocarcinoma, exploring its association with vascular-immune crosstalk and its potential as a biomarker. The authors systematically characterize EMCN expression and its clinical relevance in LUAD, building on prior GWAS links to chemotherapy-induced myelosuppression in NSCLC.

papers.title: An integrated SOX4-driven transcriptional and metabolic program governs tumor-infiltrating regulatory T cells in ovarian cancer.
papers.abstract: Regulatory T cells (Tregs) suppress antitumor immunity in ovarian cancer (OC) and are promising targets for immunotherapy. However, the heterogeneity and regulatory mechanisms of tumor-infiltrating Tregs (TI-Tregs) remain poorly defined. Here, we aim to delineate TI-Treg programs to identify potential therapeutic targets.
papers.summary: This study characterizes tumor-infiltrating regulatory T cells (TI-Tregs) in ovarian cancer and identifies SOX4 as a master regulator coordinating both transcriptional and metabolic programs that drive their immunosuppressive function. The findings suggest that targeting SOX4-driven pathways in TI-Tregs could be a promising immunotherapeutic strategy for ovarian cancer.

papers.title: OLR1 as a Key Inflammatory Regulator Associated with Poor Response to Neoadjuvant Immunochemotherapy in Resectable Lung Cancer.
papers.abstract: Poor pathological response to neoadjuvant immunotherapy combined with chemotherapy (nICT) limits long-term survival in resectable lung cancer. How to improve response rates and the regulatory mechanism of tumor inflammatory signaling in nICT efficacy remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study identifies OLR1 as a key inflammatory regulator linked to poor pathological response to neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy in resectable lung cancer. The findings suggest that OLR1-mediated inflammatory signaling may contribute to treatment resistance, highlighting a potential biomarker or therapeutic target to improve response rates.

papers.title: Association Between Mutation Context-Associated RUNX1 Transcriptional States and Immune-Stromal Heterogeneity in Nonsmall Cell Lung Cancer.
papers.abstract: Nonsmall cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is characterized by substantial heterogeneity in driver mutation backgrounds and tumor microenvironment (TME) phenotypes, yet the transcriptional regulatory states linking genotype context to immune-stromal variation remain incompletely defined. In this study, we integrated mutation, transcriptomic, and clinical data from TCGA-LUAD/LUSC to construct a mutation-expression-matched NSCLC cohort and evaluated RUNX1 as a mutation context-associated transcriptional/regulatory state rather than as a recurrently mutated driver. papers.summary: This study integrates mutation, transcriptomic, and clinical data from TCGA lung adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma cohorts to examine RUNX1 as a transcriptional regulatory state linked to specific driver mutation contexts rather than as a mutated driver gene itself. The authors find that mutation context-associated RUNX1 states correlate with immune-stromal heterogeneity in the tumor microenvironment, suggesting genotype context shapes transcriptional programs influencing immune and stromal composition in NSCLC.

papers.title: Spatial pharmacology of anti-cancer immunomodulators: a comprehensive review.
papers.abstract: The field of spatial pharmacology has emerged as a critical framework for understanding the complex interactions between anti-cancer immunomodulators, tumor cells, and the tumor microenvironment (TME) at single-cell resolution. This review synthesizes the theoretical foundations, historical evolution, clinical applications, diagnostic techniques, therapeutic strategies, and future directions of spatial pharmacology in cancer immunotherapy. By integrating single-cell analysis, signaling dynamics, and multimodal approaches, spatial pharmacology addresses the limitations of traditional "one-size-
papers.summary: This review synthesizes the emerging field of spatial pharmacology, which studies how anti-cancer immunomodulators interact with tumor cells and the tumor microenvironment at single-cell resolution. It covers theoretical foundations, historical evolution, clinical applications, diagnostic techniques, and therapeutic strategies, arguing that spatial approaches overcome the limitations of traditional one-size-fits-all cancer immunotherapy.

papers.title: Multi-omics identification and functional validation of signal regulatory protein gamma as a prognostic biomarker and immune regulator in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) comprises biologically diverse tumors, and durable responses to immune-checkpoint blockade are achieved by only a subset of patients. There remains a need for markers that connect clinical outcome with malignant-cell phenotypes and tissue-level immune organization.
papers.summary: This study uses multi-omics data to identify signal regulatory protein gamma (SIRPG) as a prognostic biomarker in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, linking its expression to patient outcomes and immune regulation. Functional validation experiments support SIRPG's role as an immune regulator, suggesting it could help stratify patients for immune-checkpoint blockade therapy.

papers.title: Integrated Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomics Reveal SERPINE1 as a Key Link Between Macro_SPP1 Macrophages and Stromal Remodeling in Gastric Cancer.
papers.abstract: Macrophage heterogeneity is increasingly recognized as an important feature of the gastric cancer tumor microenvironment, yet the macrophage states linked to poor outcome and the molecules connecting them to stromal remodeling remain incompletely defined. Here, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing data from GSE183904, spatial transcriptomic data from GSE251950, and TCGA-STAD bulk transcriptomic data to characterize macrophage diversity and identify clinically relevant macrophage-associated genes. papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell RNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics, and bulk TCGA data to characterize macrophage heterogeneity in gastric cancer, identifying a macro_SPP1 macrophage population associated with poor outcomes. Cell-cell communication analysis links these macrophages to stromal remodeling via SERPINE1, highlighting it as a potential mediator of tumor microenvironment crosstalk.

papers.title: Multi-omics analysis identifies fibroblast IGFBP5 as a key target of anti-TNFα therapy in ulcerative colitis.
papers.abstract: Resistance to anti-TNFα therapy (e.g., infliximab) in ulcerative colitis (UC) remains a significant clinical challenge, with the underlying cellular and spatial mechanisms poorly understood.
papers.summary: This study uses multi-omics analysis to investigate why some ulcerative colitis patients resist anti-TNFα therapy like infliximab. The authors identify fibroblast-derived IGFBP5 as a key target and potential mediator of treatment response, linking specific cell types to clinical outcomes. The findings suggest that targeting IGFBP5 or its pathway could help overcome therapy resistance.

papers.title: Systematic evaluation of spatial transcriptomic annotation methods reveals conserved tumor microenvironment programs in NSCLC.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) enables high-resolution mapping of cellular heterogeneity in tumor microenvironments, but downstream cell-type annotation remains highly method-dependent.
papers.summary: This study systematically benchmarks cell-type annotation methods for spatial transcriptomics data and applies them to non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) tumors. Despite method-dependent variability, the analysis identifies conserved tumor microenvironment programs across approaches, providing guidance for method selection and biological insights into NSCLC.
